_desc: R4.5/R4.5b lbt_enabled=true delivery-NEUTRALITY gate — drive via tools/dm_diff_band.py --band 0 --funnel report --min-delivery full. A single deterministic alice -> relay -> bob flow with lbt_enabled=true on every node, plus a 'spammer' node that beacons every 900ms on routing_sf (heard by alice+relay) to keep the channel intermittently busy. WHAT THIS GATE ASSERTS: lbt_enabled=true is delivery-NEUTRAL cross-engine — the LBT machinery does NOT cost a delivery; both lua and meshroute still deliver 1/1 (--band 0 + --min-delivery full forbid a per-pair delta AND a common-mode 0/N collapse). WHAT IT EXERCISES (active, not stubbed): the firmware's R4.5a LBT PRE-CHECK (tx_initiating / tx_flood checking channel_busy_until before an initiating/flood TX, then self-defer past busy_until + a backoff draw) — on seed 42 BOTH engines emit tx_lbt_defer x2. ROBUSTNESS: a single flow + 60s post-send window means alice ALWAYS completes (no competing sender to race), so this holds band-0 full across a 10-seed sweep (42/7/123/999/2024/31337/55/808/1/65535); only the funnel (defer interleaving) diverges by wire-airtime, so it is reported, not asserted. WHAT IT DOES *NOT* EXERCISE (measured — review finding): meshroute's on_radio_busy (the R4.5b SAFETY-NET retry path) NEVER fires on this gate — the R4.5a pre-check absorbs the busy channel before the sim's safety-net is reached (meshroute emits ZERO radio_busy; lua's lone radio_busy is a non-retry-eligible BCN that takes only the no-retry return). This is FUNDAMENTAL, not a tuning miss: a retry-eligible response frame (CTS/DATA/ACK does NOT pre-check LBT) only reaches on_radio_busy under strong contention, and the contention needed to force that ALSO makes delivery non-deterministic cross-engine (measured: a 150ms spammer fires meshroute on_radio_busy x2 but diverges delivery on 3/6 seeds — same non-determinism as the 2-sender race below). So the R4.5b on_radio_busy retry MECHANICS are validated by DETERMINISTIC UNIT TESTS, not this gate: blocked-DATA stash retry + retries_left 3->giveup + one rand draw per retry, the blocked-RTS re-RTS via the armed rts_timeout (PORT DIVERGENCE FIX: Lua clears awaiting_cts but its rts_timeout ignores it; ours keeps awaiting_cts so the armed timeout retries), and the DATA-retry ACK-wait re-arm (PORT DIVERGENCE FIX: Lua's on_handed re-arms; ours must too) — all in test_node_r3.cpp R4.5b. GATE REALITY (why no contention/2-sender gate): a 2-sender/1-receiver race is NON-DETERMINISTIC cross-engine — the winner depends on each engine's distinct rand stream + wire airtime, so it can legitimately resolve 2/2 on one engine and 1/2 on the other (observed: a two-direct-sender variant gave meshroute 2/2 vs lua 1/2, |d|=100pp, NEITHER buggy). Not runnable directly (nodes carry no engine/script).
